name: MITCHELL, Robert (Rob) George

headline.note: Initial chronology recovered, including roadside work omitted from the current biography. Employer identities, control and full-time evidence remain insufficient; neither headline can be calculated. Political advice and elected office are excluded.

career_spells.employer: Koala Shoes factory; exact historical payroll entity unresolved
career_spells.evidence_note: Paid trade apprenticeship is distinct from classroom study; hours unreported in the chronology. Do not presume full-time status from apprenticeship. In 2011 Hansard he recalls starting at 7.30 am and leaving at 4.30 pm during the apprenticeship. This supplies a daily span, not weekly paid hours, continuity over all four years, ; employment_status and FTE remain unknown. The2003 first speech says he completed the apprenticeship; no weekly-hours evidence. His22 March2012 parliamentary testimony explicitly names Koala Shoes as former workplace; ABC18 December2014 interview links that factory to his school-leaving apprenticeship. The later Footwear Industries Award2000 lists Koala Shoes Pty. Ltd. at169 Grange Road, Fairfield as a candidate legal identity, but cannot establish his earlier payroll entity, personal award coverage or control in1983–1987. Historical control remains unknown; no standard award hours imposed.
career_spells.counting_note: Dates, employer control and/or substantive full-time status remain insufficient for a duration calculation; unknown is not zero.

research_notes: Follow-up: identify footwear, towing/roadside and parts-supply employers; obtain public historical employment/contract evidence for hours, breaks, legal employer and control. Reconcile overlapping 1989–2000 and 1998–2000 descriptions before any calculation.

2026-09-29 initial pass: compared current APH indexed biography, 2017 Parliamentary Handbook indexed entry, full 29 September 2010 first speech, ALP biography and ABC 2013 candidate guide. Direct APH and ANU PDF opens failed; no access controls bypassed.

Targeted searches for bootmaker employer, diesel-parts employer, RACV, full-time work and agriculture adviser did not identify the missing companies or admissible hours evidence. Numerous unrelated Rob Mitchell professional profiles and overseas full-time references excluded. Repeat only with a new employer or archive lead.

Historical handbook adds 1987–1989 roadside work omitted from current APH list; omission is not evidence that work did not occur. Speech confirms sequence but cannot prove RACV was employer or fix every contract date. Transport-role titles alone do not prove private control of unidentified entities.

Campaigns in 1999, 2006 and 2007 and party participation described in first speech are political activity, not presumed paid employment. Professional membership and volunteer work likewise are not substantive paid employment. No unsupported zero or uninterrupted duration entered; initial record remains blocked.

2026-10-02 follow-up: added apprenticeship daily-hours recollection and October2007 cessation of political advisory work, qualifying the existing2006–2010 envelope. State Parliament profile confirms term and supplies 27February2003 first-speech archive lead, but legacy endpoint unavailable. Searches for footwear/diesel/parts employers and ministerial work found no company identity or weekly-hours evidence; overseas BMW, diesel social-media and medical namesakes excluded. Next: accessible Victorian2003 Hansard p56 onward for employer clues, and post-election adviser reappointment record; do not repeat generic company searches without a new lead. Both headline totals remain unknown.

2026-10-03 follow-up: a first-person 18 April 2016 parliamentary speech adds truck driving and vehicle servicing to the previously recorded transport-industry work. Its rounded '20 years' is not used to extend the dated 1987–2002 sequence, because it supplies no boundaries and conflicts with treating that 15-year envelope as exact continuous work. Added an undated, potentially overlapping spell so the work is not omitted. Targeted employer-name, diesel-parts, RACV contractor and Victorian inaugural-speech searches still did not identify a legal employer, weekly hours or the 1998/2000 transitions. Preserve the 27 February 2003 Victorian Hansard and historical company/personnel records as leads; totals remain uncalculable.

2026-10-04 follow-up: exact-phrase searches combining Rob/Robert Mitchell with bootmaking, RACV contracting, truck/bus parts and diesel-engine parts found no employer identity or personnel record. Official APH indexing repeats only the existing generic role/year chronology; derivative biographies repeat the RACV-contractor and unnamed diesel-company descriptions without a primary citation that resolves legal employer, control, hours or transitions. Broad company-name search is exhausted for this pass. The remaining productive avenues are the 27 February 2003 Victorian inaugural-speech record and historical RACV contractor/company or payroll archives; namesake transport and automotive results were excluded.

Follow-up2026-10-04: New10 February2025 first-person parliamentary testimony identifies Collingwood TAFE for apprenticeship study, previously missing. Added study separately without equating attendance dates to the1983–1987 apprenticeship or treating the provider as employer. Source says factory-floor experience but supplies no factory name or weekly hours. Official qualifications repeat the already recorded diploma/membership, with no new provider/date. State member page still routes2003 inaugural speech to the legacy tex.parliament.vic.gov.au endpoint; this pass did not recover its text. Transport employers, hours and adviser reappointment remain unresolved.

2026-10-05 original inaugural speech recovered from a modern Hansard Download PDF link after the legacy redirect and direct search-open failed. Printedp157 supplies a three-year towing recollection, requiring reconciliation with existing1987–1989 labels, and clarifies volunteer committee service. No employer, weekly hours or exact dates supplied; no date shifted. The old startpage56 link is misleading: actual speech begins printedp156. Ordinary public download/text extraction succeeded; no access controls bypassed. This closes the inaccessible-speech avenue while retaining personnel and contractor gaps.

Second targeted employer-identity pass:22March2012 first-person Hansard names Koala Shoes;18December2014 ABC interview links the factory to his school-leaving apprenticeship. Replaced unidentified footwear employer with Koala Shoes factory while retaining exact payroll identity/control and hours unknown. Later Footwear Industries Award2000 names Koala Shoes Pty.Ltd.,169GrangeRoadFairfield as a corporate lead, not personal1983–1987 coverage or historical control proof; no award hours applied. Remaining parts/towing employers, adviser return afterOctober2007 and employment continuity unresolved. Search results for US professors/financial advisers and Canadian MLA are namesakes;2016 ABC neighboring candidate university credentials not assigned to Mitchell.
